scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

problem_definition_history.requested_solution: Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.
symptoms: Dispute ticket volume rose from ~600 in June‑July to over 1,100 in August and 1,260 in September.
problem_definition_history.root_problem: Field staffing shortage causes missed manual reads (completion < target), leading to estimation substitution and incorrect bills, which drives the increase in dispute tickets.

challenges.rationale: ER-1: premise E-01 revised by E-11: Observation still shows: Field manual read completion for Aug‑Sep 2026 is 0.88 (target 0.95). No longer means: Low completion is the primary cause of estimation errors and the dispute surge; missed manual reads due to staff shortage are not the main driver of estimation errors.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

steps: read collection (AMI interval read or field manual read)
estimate substitution when no accepted read

F-01.statement: Field manual read completion for Aug‑Sep 2026 is 0.88 (target 0.95).

F-02.statement: Tariff change log contains zero records.

F-04.statement: Dispute volume monthly: June 610, July 590, August 1180, September 1260.

F-05.statement: Dispute ticket median response time 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days, SLA 3 days, total tickets 2440.

F-06.statement: Field lagging routes show completion as low as 0.7 on route R‑00.

F-07.statement: Among disputed estimated bills, 1184 had AMI read before cutoff but were rejected due to high consumption and exported to billing; 56 had no read received and were not exported.

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

CL-03.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

CL-04.statement: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

H-REQUESTER-FRAMING.statement: Dispute surge is caused by wrong bills; an AI agent that auto-answers tickets and fixes the underlying billing errors will restore baseline volume.

H-AMI-READ-ERRORS.statement: Erroneous or missing AMI reads from the MDMS lead to estimation errors and incorrect bills.

H-FIELD-READ-MISS.statement: Contracted field readers are missing scheduled manual reads, causing estimation substitution and billing errors.

H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE.statement: Recent changes to billing import validation rules introduced logic that mis‑applies tariffs or read types, generating incorrect bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Field manual read completion in Aug‑Sep is 0.88, below the 0.95 target, indicating missed reads that could lead to estimation errors.

Observation still shows: Field manual read completion for Aug‑Sep 2026 is 0.88 (target 0.95). No longer means: Low completion is the primary cause of estimation errors and the dispute surge; missed manual reads due to staff shortage are not the main driver of estimation errors.
The tariff change log shows zero records, indicating no recent tariff changes were recorded.

The observation shows that disputed bills are more frequent for actual reads (1,785) than for estimated reads (1,240), indicating that billing errors are not limited to estimation issues and that actual-read disputes constitute a larger share of the problem.
The dispute ticket volume rose sharply from ~600 in June‑July to over 1,100 in August and 1,260 in September, indicating a sustained surge rather than a transient spike.

Observation still shows: Dispute ticket volume monthly: June 610, July 590, August 1180, September 1260. No longer means: The increase in dispute volume is solely attributable to staff‑shortage‑related missed manual reads.
Dispute response times are within SLA (median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days < 3 days SLA) despite high ticket volume, indicating the surge is not driven by delayed responses.

E-06.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Staff shortage of three readers since July causes delayed routes, leading to estimated bills for affected customers.

E-07.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Indicates that no tariff change occurred this year, so tariff change cannot explain the dispute surge.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The service contract confirms that the utility can request route priority changes, but such changes require confirmation by the Field Operations Manager. This aligns with the existing K-DISPATCH constraint that route updates need runtime confirmation by SH-FIELD.

E-09.content: route-log.lagging_routes → 14 record(s); fields ['completion', 'route'] | completion: 14 distinct values | route: 14 distinct values | sample: {"completion": 0.7, "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: The observation identifies 14 lagging manual‑read routes with distinct completion values, including a sample completion of 0.7 on route R‑00, showing that some routes fall well below the 0.95 target and can cause estimation substitution.

E-10.content: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

interpretation_history.interpretation: The stakeholder reports that MDMS export access for Lakeside is now provisioned, enabling retrieval of AMI read data to investigate whether AMI read errors contribute to disputes.

The observation shows that a large subset of disputed estimated bills had AMI reads before cutoff but were rejected for high consumption (or no read received), indicating AMI read problems contribute to estimation errors.

structural_remedies.description: Reassign existing field staff to priority routes and authorize overtime to achieve the 0.95 manual read completion target (addresses the staff shortage by better utilization of current resources). Evidence: low completion (E-01), shortage statement (E-06).
structural_remedies.rationale: Can be planned and approved within the remaining ~225 minutes; requires only schedule changes and SH-FIELD runtime confirmation under K-DISPATCH.; residual gap: Does not address potential AMI read errors that could cause actual-read disputes (U-AMI-READ-ERRORS).

structural_remedies.description: Negotiate a contractual amendment with the field services vendor to guarantee minimum staffing levels (e.g., penalty for missing reads) and/or add supplemental readers. Evidence: shortage (E-06), low completion (E-01).
structural_remedies.rationale: Contract negotiations and vendor onboarding would exceed the remaining contest time; however, the change respects K-DISPATCH (requires SH-FIELD confirmation) and K-BILLWRITE (no automated bill writes).; residual gap: If staffing is increased, the root cause is removed; however, until the amendment is in place, the gap remains and may require interim dispute handling.

solution_design.why_agent: Unverified AMI read errors (U-AMI-READ-ERRORS) could cause actual-read disputes despite fixing staff shortage; an agent is needed to handle dispute tickets until that uncertainty is resolved.
solution_design.bridge_sunset_condition: If the staff reassignment (SR-R-UTIL-01) cannot be completed within the remaining contest time, the agent will continue to handle dispute tickets until the fix is in place.
